title: Token Hotspot Tracer and GPU Memory Fragmentation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, working playbook and set of lightweight scripts for isolating token-level compute hotspots and GPU memory fragmentation effects that cause latency spikes in the serving runtime. Goal is short time-to-action: reproducible captures, quick flamegraphs, basic GPU-side heuristics, and CI smoke checks that catch regressions before rollouts.

Why this is separate: existing perf docs focus on host-side stacks and heavy sampling. This doc stitches together: user-space uprobes for token boundaries, edge sampling rates tied to sequence length distributions, and a small GPU mem-fragment analyzer that complements nvidia-smi/CUPTI by correlating allocation churn with token stalls.

Key ideas / heuristics (TL;DR):
- Collect token-boundary-aware stacks: instrument LLM serving binary at the token emission point (uprobe) so we can attribute per-token latency to host/GPU call stacks.
- Use burst-adaptive sampling: higher frequency during model warm-up and at predicted long sequences; low-frequency background sampling for steady state to limit overhead.
- Generate combined flamegraphs: host stacks folded (perf) plus a lightweight GPU-time-series overlay (mem usage / kernel queue latency).
- CI smoke: generate a golden folded-stack baseline for a short synthetic trace and fail if top-N stacks change more than threshold or latency percentiles regress.

Quick components inventory (working scripts):
- token_trace_uprobe.py (python bcc script): attaches uprobes at token emission function(s) and emits token-id, timestamp, pid, tid. Also toggles high-frequency perf sampling for a short window after each long token.
- sample-flame.sh: wrapper that runs perf record/profile, runs stackcollapse-perf.pl and flamegraph.pl to produce SVG.
- gpu-memfrag-scan.sh: small helper that polls /proc/<pid>/smaps, nvml (via python-nvml) and tracks allocation/free bursts and peak fragmentation heuristic (see function below).
- ci/golden-flame-assert.py: compares folded stacks (text) against golden baseline using fuzzy matching (Levenshtein ratio + top-k stack set overlap).

Commands / examples:
- Attach token uprobe and do a 20s high-res capture:
  sudo python3 token_trace_uprobe.py --binary /opt/redwood/bin/serve --symbol emit_token --duration 20 --out token-events.log

- Perf capture (fallback if uprobes not available):
  sudo perf record -F 997 -g -p <pid> -- sleep 20
  sudo perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
  ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

- Combined run (script):
  ./sample-flame.sh --pid $PID --duration 25 --token-uprobe /opt/redwood/bin/serve:emit_token

GPU memory fragmentation heuristic (quick):
- Poll nvml memory allocations per process: record allocated_bytes and free_bytes every 100ms during capture windows.
- Track allocation churn as sum(|delta_alloc|) over window. High churn + small increases in free_bytes suggests fragmentation (lots of small frees/allocs).
- Heuristic score = churn / max(1, peak_alloc) * 1e6. Thresholds: score > 8 -> investigate. (Empirical, adjust per-card family).

Interpreting results (short):
- Flamegraph shows a tall narrow stack with host-side lock acquisition in the critical path at token boundary -> likely synchronization / lock convoys. Fixes: reduce lock scope, use lock-free ring buffers for queues.
- Flamegraph points to CUDA stream synchronization calls (cudaStreamSynchronize) invoked per-token -> likely poor batching or missing async enqueue. Fix: batch token generation calls or move sync later.
- GPU memfrag score high + tail latency spikes correlated with peak_alloc -> OSS: allocator churn from repeated small tensor allocations (FP16 quantized path often tripped). Fix: pre-allocate pooled buffers, reuse KV cache buffers, enable pooling in our allocator (see TODOs).

Runbook: triage for "token stalls > 100ms p95"
1) Reproduce: run the synthetic trace used in CI (seq len distribution matched) for 30s while collecting token_trace_uprobe and gpu-memfrag-scan at 200ms sampling.
2) Quick check: top host stacks (perf) + token events timeline. If token events show host-side wait between emit_token entry and GPU enqueue -> annotate stacks.
3) Check GPU metrics: sm_ioc latency, kernel queue length, memory utilization. If GPU kernels back up (queue len > 8) then look for slow kernel(s) or suboptimal kernel selection.
4) If memfrag score > threshold, pull a CUDAMalloc/Free histogram (we log alloc site ids from our allocator). Look for many small alloc sites in the same frame.
5) If the issue is intermittent, enable longer capture (2–5 minutes) with lower sample rate and correlate with traffic patterns.
6) Postmortem steps: create a minimal repro case (ideally pure-python tracing harness), open INF ticket with tagged stacks and heatmap screenshot, assign to serving-runtime owner.

CI integration suggestions (lightweight):
- A nightly perf-smoke job that runs synthetic trace 15s, stores folded-stacks in artifacts, and runs golden-flame-assert.py.
- A pre-merge gate triggered for PRs touching allocator/kv-cache/kernel-selection: run the smoke harness locally via ./ci/run-smoke.sh and upload artifacts to PR.
- Keep golden baseline small (only top 200 folded stacks) and use fuzzy thresholds (avoid flakiness). Store per-hardware-golden for A100/V100/RTX6000.

Implementation notes / gotchas:
- Uprobes on inlined functions: we saw emit_token inlined in optimized build. Workaround: use the public API entry that always exists (e.g., serve_token()) or build with a lightweight debug symbol set for capture builds.
- Perf overhead: 1kHz sampling on pids with many threads can add overhead; use burst windows around token events captured by bcc to limit perf window.
- eBPF stack depth: kernel vs userspace stacks sometimes mixed; ensure perf has enough unwind tables or ship a small .debug_frame for the binary used in CI.
- Permissions: captures need sudo in prod; for private deployments we use a capture helper container with CAP_SYS_ADMIN and mount proc into it.

Small example: token_trace_uprobe.py quick sketch (concept):
- attach uprobe to serve_token entry
- on entry: if seq_len >= LONG_SEQ_THRESHOLD -> start perf record subprocess with -F 997 -g -p $pid -- sleep SAMPLE_WINDOW
- emit JSON event with token_index, start_ts, perf_pid
- listen for token_index==end_token -> stop pending captures and write aggregated folded stacks

Open TODOs / experiments:
- Evaluate replacing simple nvml polling with cupti kernel timestamps to get precise per-kernel latency alignment. cupti integration is higher fidelity but much heavier and currently blocked by permissions for prod capture.
- Try a lightweight jemalloc-like arena for KV-cache allocations to reduce fragmentation; benchmark with our memfrag heuristic.
- Automate correlation: token_event timeline + perf sample timeline + nvml time series plotted together (one single SVG timeline view). Could extend flamegraph.pl to overlay time-series.
- Investigate direct GPU-side sampling (NVIDIA Nsight systems) for hard tail cases; build a cheaper public-metrics fallback if Nsight not available.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Push token_trace_uprobe.py prototype to repo under tools/tracing/token-uprobe. Add README with usage and expected permissions. (Assigned to Miguel)
- Add CI smoke harness that runs on cheapest hw flavor we support and keep golden per-hw. (Assigned to Sofia)
- Draft allocator-pooling RFC describing minimal API to expose allocation site ids into nvml logs for correlation. (Assigned to Ben)

References / links in this doc: perf/flamegraph toolchain (Brendan Gregg), BCC examples (python bcc uprobes), nvml python wrapper, internal PRs listed above. Also see confluence page for longer historical captures (link in metadata).

Last quick checklist before share:
- [ ] Clean up token_trace_uprobe logging (JSON-lines + sampling flags)
- [ ] Add CI gating script and flakiness backoffs
- [ ] Bake a short demo video for new hires showing how to run capture and read results

If you're debugging a hard tail and want help, drop a note in #eng-serving-runtime and ping @ashap. I'll try to pair on the first reproduction.

-- Asha
